entry: American actress known for romantic comedies and dramas. Roberts won the Academy Award for Best Actress for *Erin Brockovich* (2000). Her romantic comedies include *Pretty Woman* (1990), *My Best Friend's Wedding* (1997) and *Notting Hill* (1999). She was the world's highest-paid actress for most of the 1990s and the first half of the 2000s. On television, she was nominated for a Primetime Emmy Award for the [[HBO]] film *The Normal Heart* (2014). She has been the global ambassador for Lancôme since 2009.

Australian programmer and publisher who founded [[WikiLeaks]] in 2006. In 2010 WikiLeaks began publishing leaks from [[Chelsea Manning]], including U.S. military logs from the Afghanistan and Iraq wars and diplomatic cables. Assange took refuge in the Ecuadorian embassy in London in 2012 and was arrested there in 2019 after his asylum was withdrawn. The U.S. government sought his extradition on [[Espionage|Espionage Act]] charges, which critics described as an unprecedented challenge to press freedom. In 2024 he pleaded guilty in [[Saipan, Northern Mariana Islands|Saipan]] to conspiring to obtain and disclose classified U.S. defense documents, receiving a sentence of time served.

Solar calendar of 365 days, with a leap day every fourth year. It was proposed by [[Julius Caesar]] in 46 BC and took effect in 45 BC, replacing the earlier Roman calendar, a lunisolar system whose irregular intercalations had drifted out of alignment with the seasons. The Julian calendar became the predominant calendar in the [[Roman Empire]] and most of the Western world for more than 1,600 years. In 1582 Pope Gregory XIII promulgated the [[Gregorian calendar]], which eliminated occasional leap days and sharply reduced the drift. The Julian calendar's average year of 365.25 days is longer than the solar year, so it gains one day every 128 years. The [[Anno Domini]] system of numbering years was not devised until 525. Most Orthodox countries adopted the Gregorian calendar for civil use in the early 20th century but retain the Julian calendar for religious purposes.

American actress known for portraying emotionally troubled and vulnerable women. Moore won the Academy Award for Best Actress for playing an [[Alzheimer's disease|Alzheimer's]] patient in *Still Alice* (2014). She won a Primetime Emmy for playing Sarah Palin in the [[HBO]] film *Game Change* (2012). She is one of only two women to have won an acting award at each of the world's three major film festivals. Her films include *Boogie Nights* (1997), *The Hours* (2002) and *Children of Men* (2006). She has also written a series of children's books about Freckleface Strawberry.

English actress, singer, and author, known for musicals and family films. Andrews starred on Broadway as Eliza Doolittle in *My Fair Lady* (1956) and as Queen Guinevere in *Camelot* (1960). She made her film debut in the [[Walt Disney]] film *Mary Poppins* (1964), winning the Academy Award for Best Actress. The following year she played Maria von Trapp in *The Sound of Music* (1965), which won her a Golden Globe Award. Her later films included *The Princess Diaries* (2001) and voice roles in the *Shrek* franchise. She was made a Dame by [[Elizabeth II|Queen Elizabeth II]] in 2000. Her television work includes *The Julie Andrews Hour* (1973), for which she received a Primetime Emmy Award, and a voice role as Lady Whistledown in the [[Netflix]] series *Bridgerton*.

Roman imperial dynasty of the first five emperors: [[Augustus]], [[Tiberius]], [[Caligula]], [[Claudius]] and [[Nero]]. It ruled the [[Roman Empire]] from its formation under Augustus in 27 BC until Nero's suicide in AD 68. The name is a historiographical term derived from the two families of the imperial line, the *Julii Caesares* and the *Claudii Nerones*. Augustus was the adopted son of [[Julius Caesar]], and the dynasty used adoption as a tool for choosing heirs. Augustus adopted his stepson Tiberius, who was required to adopt his nephew Germanicus, father of Caligula. Claudius adopted his great-nephew and stepson Nero, who, lacking a natural or adopted son, ended the dynasty with his fall from power and suicide.

Spanish singer and songwriter, one of the best-selling recording artists in history, with more than 300 million records sold in 14 languages. Iglesias, a native of [[Madrid]], studied law and played football as a goalkeeper before a car accident in 1963 left him unable to walk for two years. While recovering in hospital, he was given a guitar and discovered his musical talent. He won the 1968 Benidorm Song Festival and represented [[Spain]] at the Eurovision Song Contest in 1970 with the song "Gwendolyne," finishing fourth. He has performed more than 5,000 concerts and has had a star on the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]] since 1985. [[UNICEF]] named him Special Ambassador for the Performing Arts in 1989.

Tanzanian politician and political theorist who led [[Tanzania]] as president from 1964 to 1985. Nyerere helped form the Tanganyika African National Union (TANU) in 1954, and TANU won the 1960 general election under his leadership. He became prime minister of Tanganyika in 1961 and its first president in 1962. Influenced by [[Mahatma Gandhi]], he preached non-violent protest. After Zanzibar was unified with Tanganyika in 1964, he promoted *Ujamaa*, a form of African socialism set out in the 1967 Arusha Declaration, which nationalized banks and major industries and formed communal farms. These reforms hampered food production. He built a one-party state and developed close links with [[Mao Zedong]]'s China. Tanzania's 1978–1979 war with Uganda overthrew [[Idi Amin]]. He is described in Tanzania as the "Father of the Nation," though critics cited his use of detention without trial.

American couple convicted of spying for the [[Soviet Union]]. They provided top-secret information about American [[Radar|radar]], [[Sonar|sonar]], jet propulsion engines, and nuclear weapon designs. They were executed at Sing Sing in New York, the first American civilians executed for such charges and the first executed during peacetime. Decoded Soviet cables from the Venona project, declassified after the Soviet Union's fall, detailed Julius's role as a courier and recruiter. For decades, supporters including their sons sought exoneration. The sons later acknowledged Julius's involvement while maintaining that Ethel was innocent.

Second French revolution, also called *les Trois Glorieuses* (the Three Glorious Days), in which King Charles X, the French [[House of Bourbon|Bourbon]] monarch, was overthrown in 1830. His cousin Louis Philippe, Duke of Orléans, became king and governed for 18 years as the last king of France. Critics had accused Charles X of pandering to the Catholic Church and of violating the equality of religious belief guaranteed by the Charter of 1814. The revolution restored [[Constitutional monarchy|constitutional monarchy]] under the July Monarchy, ended the Bourbons' rule in favor of their cadet branch, the House of Orléans, and replaced hereditary right with popular sovereignty. Louis Philippe was overthrown in the French Revolution of 1848.

Form of locomotion in which an [[Organism|organism]] or robotic system propels itself through the air along a ballistic trajectory. Jumping is distinguished from [[Running|running]] by the long aerial phase and high angle of launch. Kangaroos use hopping as their primary locomotion, while frogs jump mainly to escape predators. All jumping requires force against a substrate, such as ground or water, and muscles add [[Kinetic energy|kinetic energy]] to the body during launch. Many jumping animals have long legs, and some store energy in elastic [[Tendon|tendons]] before takeoff to release it at a higher power than muscle alone. A running jump adds horizontal velocity, so jumpers travel farther when starting from a run. Jumping is also central to the [[Long jump]], [[High jump]] and show jumping.

Spider of the family Salticidae, the largest spider family, with almost 700 genera and around 7,000 described [[Species|species]]. Jumping spiders have some of the best vision among [[Arthropod|arthropods]] and use sight in courtship, hunting and navigation. Most species move unobtrusively but can make agile jumps, especially when hunting or escaping sudden threats. All have four pairs of eyes, and the large anterior median pair provides detailed vision that helps the spider aim its leaps. They are generally recognized by their eye pattern. Silk safety lines anchor them while they jump, and they build silken "pup tents" for shelter, where they molt and store egg cases. Body length generally ranges from 1 to 25 mm (0.04–0.98 in), and the largest species is *Hyllus giganteus*.

Japanese writer and composer, co-founder of the visual novel brand Key under Visual Arts. Maeda is considered a pioneer of *nakige* visual novels. He wrote the scenarios and music for most Key games, including the majority of *Air* and *Clannad*. He also served as screenwriter and composer for anime series produced by P.A. Works, such as *Angel Beats!* and *Charlotte*. In high school he became immersed in the [[Fantasy|fantasy]] genre and began writing lyrics and music.

Genus of [[Monocotyledon|monocotyledonous]] [[Flowering plant|flowering plants]] commonly known as rushes. It is the largest genus in the family Juncaceae, with around 340 species. Rushes superficially resemble grasses or sedges, but their flowers and round stems distinguish them. The genus is nearly cosmopolitan, found on every continent except [[Antarctica]], and typically grows in cold or wet habitats such as salt marshes and seeps. Juncus species provide food and habitat for microbes, insects, amphibians, fish and birds. Research suggests that strategic planting may help clean contaminated water. Fibrous stems have been used for cordage, baskets and candle wicks. The genus was first named by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in his 1753 *Species Plantarum*.

City (pop., 2025: 31,454), capital of [[Alaska]] on the Gastineau Channel. It became the capital in 1906, when the government moved there from Sitka. The consolidated City and Borough of Juneau is larger than [[Rhode Island]] and [[Delaware]]. It is one of only two U.S. state capitals with no road connection to the rest of its state or to the contiguous United States, the other being [[Honolulu]]. Cruise ships bring 16,000 or more visitors a day from May to September, generating $375 million in direct spending in 2023.

Land covered with dense forest and tangled vegetation, usually in [[Tropical climate|tropical climates]]. The word derives from the [[Sanskrit]] *jaṅgala*, meaning rough and arid, and entered English in the 18th century through Hindustani. In its strict sense, a jungle is ground-level vegetation so dense that travelers must cut their way through, which distinguishes it from a [[Rainforest|rainforest]], whose understory is usually open. Monsoon forests and [[Mangrove|mangroves]] are often called jungles in this sense. In a looser sense, jungle has meant any humid tropical forest, a usage largely replaced by "tropical forest" and "rainforest" since the 1970s. As a metaphor, the word describes lawless or unruly situations, as in Upton Sinclair's *The Jungle* (1906), about workers at the Chicago Stockyards.

Genus of coniferous [[Tree|trees]] and [[Shrub|shrubs]] in the cypress family, with between 50 and 67 species, depending on taxonomic authority. Junipers are widely distributed throughout the [[Northern Hemisphere]]. The highest known juniper forest, at 4,900 m (16,100 ft), grows in southeastern [[Tibet]] and the northern [[Himalayas]]. Junipers are [[Gymnosperm|gymnosperms]] with needle-like or scale-like leaves. Most species have blue, berrylike seed cones, which are aromatic and can be used as a spice, most famously in gin. Seeds take 1–3 years to develop, and their hard coats let them pass through the digestive systems of birds and mammals undamaged, which disperses them.

Chief deity of the Roman state religion, god of the sky and thunder, and king of the gods, also known as Jove. He was the central guardian of the state in the Capitoline Triad, with Juno and Minerva, and many of his functions centered on the Capitoline Hill. His identifying symbols were the thunderbolt and the [[Eagle|eagle]], and his sacred tree was the [[Oak|oak]]. The Romans regarded him as the equivalent of the Greek [[Zeus]], and in [[Latin literature|Latin literature]] and Roman art, the myths and iconography of Zeus were adapted under the name Jupiter. Consuls swore their oaths of office in his name, and triumphal generals surrendered the tokens of victory at his statue on the Capitol. Roman decisions were guided by auguries, the signs read from lightning and bird flight.

1993 American science fiction film directed by [[Steven Spielberg]] and based on the novel by [[Michael Crichton]]. It follows visitors to a dinosaur theme park on the fictional island of Isla Nublar off [[Costa Rica]], after sabotage disables the park's security systems. Its computer-generated dinosaurs are widely seen as a turning point for visual effects, and the film won three Academy Awards. It grossed over $914 million in its original run, becoming the highest-grossing film of all time until *Titanic*. It spawned six sequels.

Geologic period of the [[Mesozoic]] Era, lasting about 58.3 million years, from 201.4 to 143.1 million years ago. It is named after the Jura Mountains, where limestone strata from the period were first identified. The Jurassic began with the [[Triassic–Jurassic extinction|Triassic–Jurassic extinction event]], associated with the eruption of the Central Atlantic Magmatic Province. By its start, the supercontinent [[Pangaea]] had begun rifting into Laurasia and [[Gondwana]], and the climate was warmer than today, with no ice caps. Dinosaurs became the dominant land animals, and the first stem-group birds evolved from theropod dinosaurs. Marine reptiles such as ichthyosaurs and [[Plesiosaur|plesiosaurs]] inhabited the oceans, and modern sharks, rays and [[Teleost|teleost]] fish first appeared. The end of the Jurassic has no clear boundary with the [[Cretaceous]], the only boundary between geological periods to remain formally undefined.

Philosophy of [[Law|law]], also called legal theory or legal science. It applies philosophical methods to questions such as what the law is and how it ought to be. Thinkers including [[Confucius]] and [[Aristotle]] wrote on law, and contemporary academic jurisprudence traces its origin to the early 17th century and the [[Age of Enlightenment]]. Among the oldest conceptions of law are natural law theories, instrumental theories, and law as an expression of social norms and custom. In the 20th century, the legal positivism of H. L. A. Hart and Hans Kelsen became dominant. General jurisprudence asks what law is and what characteristics it has in every jurisdiction, while normative jurisprudence evaluates law philosophically. In civil law jurisdictions, the term refers to case law or precedent.

Sworn body of people, called jurors, convened to hear evidence in a [[Trial|trial]] and render an impartial verdict. The jury system developed in England during the [[Middle Ages]] and is a hallmark of [[Common law|common law]] systems. Juries are commonly used in countries with legal systems derived from the British Empire, such as the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, Australia and Ireland. Most other countries, whose legal systems derive from European civil law or [[Sharia|Islamic sharia law]], usually determine guilt with a single professional judge. Most trial juries, called petit juries, have up to 15 members. Grand juries, used mostly in U.S. federal courts and some state jurisdictions, have between 16 and 23 members and decide whether there is enough evidence for a criminal trial to go forward. Under the Fifth Amendment, federal charges for "capital, or otherwise infamous" crimes require a grand jury indictment.

Canadian singer, one of the best-selling music artists of all time, with estimated sales of over 150 million records. Discovered by talent manager Scooter Braun in the late 2000s, Bieber became a teen idol after his EP *My World* (2009). His debut studio album, *My World 2.0* (2010), topped the U.S. Billboard 200, making him the youngest solo male to do so in 47 years. His album *Purpose* (2015) yielded three Billboard Hot 100 number-one singles. He has won two [[Grammy Awards]] and was named by [[Time (magazine)|Time]] as one of the 100 most influential people in 2011.

American singer, songwriter, and actor, a former member of [[NSYNC]]. Dubbed the "Prince of Pop," he rose to fame as a child on *Star Search* and in the [[Disney Channel]] series *The All New Mickey Mouse Club*. His solo album *FutureSex/LoveSounds* (2006) produced the chart-topping singles "SexyBack" and "My Love." His next three albums, including *The 20/20 Experience* (2013) and *Man of the Woods* (2018), all peaked atop the U.S. Billboard 200. He has won 10 [[Grammy Awards]] and voiced Branch in the *Trolls* franchise.

Canadian politician, prime minister of [[Canada]] from 2015 to 2025. The son of Prime Minister [[Pierre Trudeau]], he led the Liberal Party from 2013 and led it to a majority government in the 2015 federal election. His government legalized recreational cannabis and medical assistance in dying and introduced a federal carbon tax. It resettled refugees of the [[Syrian civil war]] and signed the Paris Agreement on climate change. Trudeau was found twice by the ethics commissioner to have violated conflict of interest law. Amid declining popular support, he announced in January 2025 that he would resign as prime minister and Liberal leader.
